doc.title: Jerry Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe and Christian Goodwillie, via Zoom, June 30, 2021

title: Kind of Blue and Chico Hamilton's Man from Two Worlds
summary: The two first jazz albums he bought were Kind of Blue and Chico Hamilton's 'Man from Two Worlds' with Charles Lloyd; talk of Lloyd's records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I have a guess, I’ll let Monk go first.
That’s what I was going to guess too.
All right well you guys are winners.

That was one of them okay. He handed me that in mono, and the other one you won’t guess but it’s an album that rearranged my DNA for the rest of my life and it remains rearranged to this point, and that was Chico Hamilton “Man from Two Worlds” on Impulse, musical director Charles Lloyd.
Ah. I was going to guess Charles Lloyd as the second one so I was close.

Yup. The musical director Charles Lloyd. It had “Forest Flower” on it, it had guitarist, excuse me Gabor Szabo who played psychedelically you know, he had been a Hungarian freedom fighter when the Russians came into Hungary and then he split. So there is an Eastern influence on his guitar, the music was great. So that was it. Those two records, they are what, those are two desert island discs and they set me off into my career in jazz.
That’s awesome. I’m going to check out that Chico Hamilton. The reason I was going to guess Charles Lloyd is —
Yeah I can’t figure that, why you did.

Well only because the covers of some of those records like “At the Love In” I think and you know, they’ve got this psychedelic rock style covers so I would think it would be enticing if you were coming from Vanilla Fudge or, you know, Iron Butterfly or something.

Absolutely. But those were not the great Charles Lloyd albums. I liked Charles Lloyd with Chico Hamilton. There is a series of great Chico Hamilton records. I liked Charles Lloyd “Live at Monterey” that was another classic on Atlantic with Keith Jarrett on piano, a young Keith Jarrett. So yeah, those psychedelic ones were cool looking but the great, to me, the great Charles Lloyd albums preceded those, plus his records on Columbia.
Yup. But you need them, Christian.
Well thank God I have a Spotify subscription ‘cause like you I see the dollar sale ad and I’m a beeline to the record store, so I rarely have spare money.
Yeah well you won’t be disappointed with “Man from Two Worlds.”
